All 19 tests pass, including the ignored ones (verified with `-- --include-ignored`).

Implementation in `src/lib.rs`:
- `under_hundred` — spells 0–99, hyphenating tens and ones (e.g. `twenty-two`).
- `under_thousand` — spells 0–999 with the "hundred" part.
- `encode(n: u64)` — splits the number into 3-digit chunks from the right, attaches scale words (`thousand` … `quintillion`), skips zero chunks, and joins with spaces. Since the input type is `u64`, out-of-range values (like -1) can't be represented, satisfying the Rust-specific note. It also covers the extension case up to `u64::MAX` (the `max_u64` test).
